title: Babson, Louis Witten and Bryce DeWitt gravity institutes
place_text: Johns Hopkins; University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill

tellings.quote: Babson contacted Louis Witten, who was coming out of Johns Hopkins,

plain: In the 1950s a man named Babson, who funded research on gravity, is said to have approached the physicist Louis Witten, then coming out of Johns Hopkins, and helped set up gravity research institutes, with the physicist Bryce DeWitt's work at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The researcher Eric Weinstein tells this to Michels, saying "Babson contacted Louis Witten, who was coming out of Johns Hopkins," without naming a source. It comes up because those years are said to be when serious interest in antigravity began.
